export const meta = {
  name: 'ajcr-w4-rep-recon',
  description: 'Deep parallel recon of the six blocking fronts of Pic^0 representability, adversarially verified',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Recon', detail: 'one agent per blocking front, read-only' },
    { title: 'Verify', detail: 'adversarial check of each front\u2019s key claim' },
  ],
}

const ROOT = '/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon'
const PROJ = ROOT + '/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild'

const COMMON = `
You are doing READ-ONLY reconnaissance inside an Archon Horizon Lean 4 workspace.
Workspace root: ${ROOT}
Project (cwd for all work): ${PROJ}
Another horizon run (0046) is LIVE on this workspace. Therefore:
  * DO NOT edit, write or commit ANY file. Read-only. No lake build. No lake env lean.
  * You MAY use the lean-lsp MCP tools (lean_goal, lean_hover_info, lean_declaration_file,
    lean_diagnostic_messages, lean_loogle, lean_leansearch, lean_file_outline) \u2014 these are cheap.
  * You MAY use: /home/axel/.archon-env/bin/horizon search "<words>" --json --root ${ROOT}
    which indexes THIS project, the sibling project MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge,
    and all of mathlib. USE IT rather than grep when hunting for a lemma you cannot name.
    grep is fine for finding a known string / all call sites.

BACKGROUND \u2014 what this project is trying to do.
The target is \`AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian\` (AlgebraicJacobian/Challenge.lean:96-99, a bare \`sorry\`).
The route is Wave 4: representability of Pic^0 via a curve-specialised Kleiman argument.
A previous session established (all kernel-checked, 0 sorries) that the DD-R relative-divisor
certificate interface \`DivisorAdaptation.IsCertified\` is satisfiable for a CONNECTED divisor
ONLY IF that divisor lies inside a single pinned chart of \`\u03c0\` (i.e. avoids \u03c0\u207b\u00b9(0) or avoids
\u03c0\u207b\u00b9(\u221e)). See AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivSchemeCertZarChartTrace.lean,
DivSchemeCertZarSwallow.lean, DivSchemeCertZarConn.lean, DivSchemeCertZarC1.lean and
informal/spec-dd-r.md ADDENDUM 2.
The roadmap node AJCR.w4-rep (read ${ROOT}/.archon-horizon/roadmap/items/AJCR.w4-rep.yaml)
says there are SIX INDEPENDENT MOUNTAINS before Challenge.lean:99.

YOUR OUTPUT IS DATA, not prose for a human. Be specific: exact file:line, exact declaration
names, exact signatures. Distinguish sharply between:
  (i) what is PROVED in Lean today (name it, say which file:line, say if it has sorries),
  (ii) what is STATED but unproved / sorried,
  (iii) what exists only in informal/*.md prose,
  (iv) what does not exist at all.
Never say "should be easy" without naming the exact lemma that would do it.
`

const FRONT_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  additionalProperties: false,
  required: ['front', 'verdict', 'summary', 'existing', 'missing', 'nextActions', 'keyClaim'],
  properties: {
    front: { type: 'string' },
    verdict: {
      type: 'string',
      enum: ['tractable-now', 'tractable-after-one-lemma', 'needs-design-decision', 'large-but-launchable', 'genuinely-blocked'],
    },
    summary: { type: 'string', description: 'What is actually true about this front, 5-15 sentences, concrete.' },
    existing: {
      type: 'array',
      description: 'Declarations that ALREADY EXIST and are proved, usable as inputs.',
      items: {
        type: 'object',
        additionalProperties: false,
        required: ['name', 'fileLine', 'signature', 'proved'],
        properties: {
          name: { type: 'string' },
          fileLine: { type: 'string' },
          signature: { type: 'string' },
          proved: { type: 'boolean' },
        },
      },
    },
    missing: {
      type: 'array',
      description: 'What must be built. Each entry MUST be a precise Lean-ready statement, not a wish.',
      items: {
        type: 'object',
        additionalProperties: false,
        required: ['name', 'statement', 'size', 'blockedBy'],
        properties: {
          name: { type: 'string' },
          statement: { type: 'string', description: 'Lean-ready or near-Lean statement of the obligation' },
          size: { type: 'string', enum: ['S', 'M', 'L', 'XL'] },
          blockedBy: { type: 'string', description: 'empty string if nothing blocks it' },
        },
      },
    },
    nextActions: {
      type: 'array',
      description: 'Ordered, concrete, each doable in one session by one agent.',
      items: { type: 'string' },
    },
    keyClaim: {
      type: 'string',
      description: 'The single most load-bearing factual claim you are making, phrased so it can be independently refuted.',
    },
  },
}

const FRONTS = [
  {
    key: 'chart-avoid',
    label: 'chart-avoid (THE decision)',
    prompt: `
FRONT 1 \u2014 CHART-AVOID. This is the highest-value question in the whole project. Read
informal/spec-dd-r.md, especially ADDENDUM 1 and ADDENDUM 2 (lines 370-483), in full.

THE QUESTION: **Does the \`Z(\u2666)\` chart confine its divisors to a single pinned chart of \`\u03c0\`?**

spec-dd-r.md ADDENDUM 2 \u00a74 (line 477-479) gives a concrete lead and calls it "the tractable
half of the yes-case":

  "K \u2286 H\u2070(\u0398\u1d43) with \u0398 = \u03c0\u207b\u00b9(\u221e), and a generator of exact pole order \`a\` has no zero on \u0398,
   so \`supportLocus \u2229 \u03c0\u207b\u00b9(\u221e) = \u2205\` should follow from the seed's own exactness data."

YOUR JOB: determine whether that lead is REAL \u2014 i.e. whether the theta-avoidance
\`supportLocus \u2229 \u03c0\u207b\u00b9(\u221e) = \u2205\` is derivable IN LEAN from data the DD-R seed ALREADY carries.

Do this concretely:
 1. Find \`Z(\u2666)\` in Lean. Find the DD-R seed structure and the universal family. Look at
    AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivSchemeCertSeed.lean, DivSchemeCertUniv.lean,
    DivSchemeCertZarSeed.lean. Also \`horizon search\` for "Diamond", "Zdiamond", "seed",
    "universal family", "windowS", "WindowLedger", "poleOrder", "HighWindow".
 2. Write down the EXACT structure fields the seed carries \u2014 every hypothesis available.
    Quote the actual Lean \`structure\` declaration.
 3. Find \`fiberTwoCover\`, \`relCover\`, \`V\u2080\`, \`V\u2081\`, and identify precisely WHICH of V\u2080/V\u2081 is
    \u03c0\u207b\u00b9(0)-avoiding and which is \u03c0\u207b\u00b9(\u221e)-avoiding, and how \`supportLocus\` relates to them.
    Find \`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.supportLocus\` (Picard/SupportTube.lean:131).
 4. Answer: does the seed carry the exact-pole-order / no-zero-on-\u0398 datum, in ANY form?
    If yes, name the field. If it carries something weaker, say exactly what and what the gap is.
 5. If the datum is NOT there: is it a legitimate ADDITION to the seed (i.e. does the actual
    mathematics of the Z(\u2666) construction supply it, so adding the field is honest bookkeeping),
    or would adding it be assuming the conclusion? This distinction is the whole decision.
    Note spec-dd-r.md \u00a7Discipline (2) forbids "support-separation hypotheses" \u2014 read that line
    (around line 360) and judge whether the theta-avoidance datum violates it or is different
    in kind (a property of the SEED's construction vs. an assumption on an ARBITRARY divisor).
 6. Also read informal/spec-dd-2.md and any worksheet on Z(\u2666) if present (ls informal/).

Your \`missing\` array must contain the precise Lean statement(s) that would settle chart-avoid.
Your \`keyClaim\` must be a yes/no answer to "is theta-avoidance derivable from landed seed data?"
`,
  },
  {
    key: 'divrep',
    label: 'divrep (no producers)',
    prompt: `
FRONT 2 \u2014 DIVREP. The roadmap says: "DivRepAffinePullback (4 fields) and DivRepGlobalData
(5 fields) have ZERO producers anywhere in the tree; no \`def divRep\` / \`divRepAff\` exists.
Three of the four affine fields are pre-certificate launchable (the two inverse laws +
naturality)."

YOUR JOB:
 1. Find \`DivRepAffinePullback\` and \`DivRepGlobalData\`. Quote both structures IN FULL with
    every field's type. Give file:line.
 2. Confirm or refute "zero producers": search for any \`def\`/\`instance\`/\`theorem\` that
    CONSTRUCTS a term of either type. Also look for \`divRep\`, \`divRepAff\`, \`RepresentableBy\`,
    \`divFunctor\`, \`DivScheme\`, \`DivFamZar\`, \`IsLocallyCertified\`.
 3. For EACH field of \`DivRepAffinePullback\`, say precisely: what would have to be proved,
    whether it depends on the certificate lane (i.e. on \`IsCertified\`), and what already-landed
    lemma is its nearest input. Identify exactly which three fields are "pre-certificate
    launchable" and verify that claim yourself.
 4. Look at all files matching AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivRep*.lean (there are several) and
    report what each contains and whether it is sorried.
 5. Read informal/spec-dd-r.md \u00a73 item 8 and \u00a74 for the pinned deliverable shapes.
Your \`missing\` entries should be the individual field obligations, each with a Lean-ready
statement, so a later agent can pick one up cold.
`,
  },
  {
    key: 'c9-chartlocus',
    label: 'C9 chartLocus',
    prompt: `
FRONT 3 \u2014 DAT-C C9 / chartLocus. The roadmap says: "\`chartLocus\` (Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:162-164)
has ZERO hits tree-wide, yet four roadmap comments call the remainder 'C9-gated plumbing, no
math left'. It is the sole gate of dat-b B-6 AND of the whole dat-glue assembly: the
highest-leverage single row outside DD-R."

YOUR JOB:
 1. Read AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean around line 162 \u2014 quote \`chartLocus\` and
    its surrounding context in full. What is it FOR?
 2. Verify the "zero hits" claim (grep the whole project for \`chartLocus\`).
 3. Read the roadmap items ${ROOT}/.archon-horizon/roadmap/items/AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-c*.yaml
    and AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-b.yaml and AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-glue.yaml (cat them), plus the
    comments under ${ROOT}/.archon-horizon/roadmap/comments/ for those ids.
 4. Read the informal spec for dat-c (ls informal/ and find it; likely spec-dat-c*.md or
    spec-w4-gates.md).
 5. Determine what C9 actually is, what its precise Lean obligation is, and whether "plumbing,
    no math left" is TRUE or wishful. Give the exact Lean statement(s) still owed.
 6. Say precisely what dat-b B-6 and dat-glue need FROM C9.
`,
  },
  {
    key: 'colimit',
    label: 'Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit',
    prompt: `
FRONT 4 \u2014 Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit. The roadmap calls this the "CHEAPEST REAL ADVANCE
OFF THE CERTIFICATE PATH: (PicRepColimitCompat.lean:136) \u2014 explicitly divRep-free, mathlib
avatars pinned, reduction landed, nothing blocking it."

YOUR JOB:
 1. Read AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/PicRepColimitCompat.lean IN FULL (or at least the whole
    region around line 136 plus the file header/outline). Quote the target statement exactly.
 2. What is sorried? What is proved? List every \`sorry\` in the file with its goal
    (use lean_goal at the sorry position via the lean-lsp MCP).
 3. What are the "mathlib avatars pinned"? Name them and CHECK they exist in the current
    mathlib (use \`horizon search\` / lean_loogle / lean_hover_info). Mathlib moves \u2014 a pin
    recorded weeks ago may be stale.
 4. Also look for the related DAT-G0.beta1 material: "pic0 commutes with the base-field
    filtered colimit", informal/spec-datg0.md \u00a74.3 (read that section). The roadmap calls
    beta1 "the ONE genuinely undesigned mathematical question of the endgame". Is
    Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit the same thing as beta1, or a different (easier) statement?
    This matters a lot \u2014 be precise.
 5. Give the exact proof plan: which mathlib lemma chain closes it. Be concrete enough that an
    agent can start typing.
`,
  },
  {
    key: 'build-reach',
    label: 'build-reach (95 modules)',
    prompt: `
FRONT 5 \u2014 BUILD REACH. The roadmap says: "95 modules (every DivRep*/HighWindow*/Redesign* file)
sit outside lake's default target, and DivRepAffKitZar.lean has no olean at all \u2014 see the
build-reach row." Roadmap item id: AJCR.w4-rep.build-reach (cat
${ROOT}/.archon-horizon/roadmap/items/AJCR.w4-rep.build-reach.yaml).

This matters because a module outside the default build is NOT verified by the aggregator, so
"landed, kernel-checked" claims about it may be false.

YOUR JOB (still READ-ONLY \u2014 do not build, do not edit):
 1. Read AlgebraicJacobian.lean (the root aggregator) and lakefile.toml. Work out exactly what
    the default target imports.
 2. Compute the precise list of .lean files under AlgebraicJacobian/ that are NOT reachable by
    import from the root aggregator. Do this by parsing imports, e.g. with a python script that
    builds the import graph from the \`import \` lines and does a reachability search from
    \`AlgebraicJacobian\`. Report the COUNT and the full list grouped by directory/prefix.
 3. Check which of those unreachable modules have a stale-or-missing olean under .lake/build/lib
    (just \`ls\`/\`find\`, do not build).
 4. CRITICALLY: cross-check against the roadmap's claim that two of the unreachable modules are
    "cited by the roadmap as landed inputs". Which ones? Are any of the certificate-lane files
    (Picard/DivSchemeCert*.lean) or the files named in the recent commits
    (DivSchemeCertZarChartTrace, DivSchemeCertZarSwallow, DivSchemeCertZarConn,
    DivSchemeCertZarC1, DivSchemeCertZarChartPair) unreachable? Say yes/no per file. This is
    the load-bearing part: if those are unreachable, the "kernel-checked, in the default build"
    claims in the last session's report are wrong.
 5. Report the exact minimal set of \`import\` lines that would need to be added to the root to
    fix reachability, and flag any that would likely CONFLICT (duplicate public declarations \u2014
    a known hazard: the same helper lemma was re-declared 13\u00d7 across the tree by parallel lanes,
    which passes per-module builds but breaks the aggregator). Use grep to find duplicate
    top-level declaration names across the unreachable set.
`,
  },
  {
    key: 'dat-g',
    label: 'dat-g (true bottleneck)',
    prompt: `
FRONT 6 \u2014 DAT-G, plus the overall shape of the endgame. The roadmap calls dat-g "no spec, no
worksheet, no Lean file, unfrozen handoff shape \u2014 the true bottleneck".

YOUR JOB:
 1. cat ${ROOT}/.archon-horizon/roadmap/items/AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-g.yaml and
    AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-j.yaml and AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-b.yaml and
    AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-glue.yaml and AJCR.w4-rep.datum.yaml. Also the comments dirs for them.
 2. Read informal/spec-w4-gates.md IN FULL \u2014 the roadmap calls its "corrected full map" the
    master plan. Reproduce that map faithfully in your summary: what are the gates, in what
    order, and which are done.
 3. Determine what dat-g actually has to produce (a Lean statement / structure), what consumes
    it, and whether ANY Lean exists for it. Search the SIBLING project
    MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge (the older, read-only one) for the same
    material \u2014 \`horizon search\` covers it. If the old project already did this, that is a
    major lead: say exactly which declarations and where.
 4. Give an honest ordering of the six mountains by (leverage \u00d7 tractability), and say which
    single one a competent agent should attack next to move Challenge.lean:99.
 5. Also report: how many \`sorry\`s are in the project total, and where the biggest clusters are
    (\`grep -rn "sorry" AlgebraicJacobian/ --include=*.lean | wc -l\` and a breakdown by file,
    excluding comments/docstrings as best you can).
`,
  },
]

phase('Recon')

const results = await pipeline(
  FRONTS,
  (f) => agent(COMMON + f.prompt, {
    label: `recon:${f.key}`,
    phase: 'Recon',
    schema: FRONT_SCHEMA,
  }),
  (r, f) => {
    if (!r) return null
    return agent(
      COMMON + `
FRONT UNDER REVIEW: ${f.label}

A recon agent examined this front and made the following LOAD-BEARING CLAIM:

  "${r.keyClaim}"

with verdict "${r.verdict}" and this summary:

${r.summary}

and these "missing" obligations:
${JSON.stringify(r.missing, null, 1)}

YOUR JOB IS TO REFUTE IT. Go to the actual Lean and the actual files and check. Default to
\`refuted: true\` if you cannot positively confirm the claim against real source. Specifically:
  * Does every declaration it cites as EXISTING actually exist, at that file:line, with that
    signature, and is it genuinely sorry-free? Check at least the three most load-bearing ones
    by reading the source (grep the name, read the surrounding lines) \u2014 do not trust the
    search index alone, and check for \`sorry\`/\`admit\`/\`native_decide\` in the proof body.
  * Is any "missing" obligation actually ALREADY PROVED somewhere (including in the sibling
    project MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge, or in mathlib)? Use \`horizon search\`.
  * Is the verdict too optimistic \u2014 does a cited "next action" secretly depend on something
    that does not exist?
  * Is the verdict too PESSIMISTIC \u2014 is there a route the recon agent missed?
Report corrections precisely with file:line evidence.
`,
      {
        label: `verify:${f.key}`,
        phase: 'Verify',
        schema: {
          type: 'object',
          additionalProperties: false,
          required: ['front', 'refuted', 'confidence', 'corrections', 'confirmedFacts', 'missedRoutes'],
          properties: {
            front: { type: 'string' },
            refuted: { type: 'boolean' },
            confidence: { type: 'string', enum: ['low', 'medium', 'high'] },
            corrections: {
              type: 'array',
              items: { type: 'string' },
              description: 'Each with file:line evidence. Empty if none.',
            },
            confirmedFacts: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
            missedRoutes: {
              type: 'array',
              items: { type: 'string' },
              description: 'Routes the recon agent did not consider that look viable.',
            },
          },
        },
      },
    ).then((v) => ({ front: f.key, recon: r, verify: v }))
  },
)

const clean = results.filter(Boolean)
log(`recon complete on ${clean.length}/${FRONTS.length} fronts`)
return clean

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivSchemeCertZarTransport

/-!
# The chart-confinement obstruction in witness form

`DivSchemeCertZarC1.lean` establishes the verdict positively: a certified adaptation of a
connected divisor confines its support to one pinned chart
(`supportLocus_subset_chart_of_isCertified`).  Its contrapositive is recorded there only for
the *leak-free* hypothesis and only in "not contained in either chart" form.

This file states the obstruction in the form a would-be user of the interface meets it: with
two **witness points** of the support, one off `V₀` and one off `V₁`.  That is the shape in
which a concrete divisor — e.g. one whose fibre over a base point is `{0, ∞}` — refutes
certifiability, and it needs no leak hypothesis.

Combined with the pullback transport (`DivSchemeCertZarTransport.lean`), which shows support
loci pull back along the base-shrinking maps, the obstruction is visibly Zariski-local on the
base: shrinking cannot separate the two witnesses.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.not_isCertified_of_isPreconnected_of_witnesses` — a
  connected divisor with a support point off each pinned chart admits no certified adaptation,
  in any degree.
-/

outside `V₀` and a point outside `V₁` — i.e. the divisor genuinely meets both `pi⁻¹(∞)` and

(`supportLeak_eq_empty_of_finite_colength`).  So the interface does not merely make such

rw [Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ_eq_mk, Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr hmem, zero_mul])

/-- The product of the chart-local colength modules (an `abbrev`, so the `Pi.module`
instances apply directly — probe finding, spec §1b(iii)). -/
noncomputable abbrev chartProd : Type u := ∀ j : A.index, A.colength j

/-- The product of the overlap colength modules over ordered index pairs. -/
noncomputable abbrev ovlProd : Type u := ∀ p : A.index × A.index, A.ovlColength p.1 p.2

/-- The left arrow of the equalizer: restrict the `p.1` component to each overlap. -/
noncomputable def deltaLeft : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
  LinearMap.pi
    (fun p : A.index × A.index => (A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.1)

/-- The right arrow of the equalizer: restrict the `p.2` component to each overlap. -/
noncomputable def deltaRight : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
  LinearMap.pi
    (fun p : A.index × A.index => (A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.2)

/-- **The glued colength module `W(d)`** (worksheet §1.1 (c2)): the equalizer of the two
overlap-restriction arrows on the product of chart-local colengths, spelled as the
kernel of their difference (so the `FlatCokernel` base-change keystone applies
verbatim); the equalizer description is `mem_gluedSubmodule_iff`. -/
noncomputable def gluedSubmodule : Submodule R A.chartProd :=
  LinearMap.ker (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight)

/-- The equalizer description of the glued colength module: componentwise agreement of
the two overlap restrictions. -/
lemma mem_gluedSubmodule_iff (s : A.chartProd) :
    s ∈ A.gluedSubmodule ↔ ∀ p : A.index × A.index,
      A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2 (s p.1) = A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2 (s p.2) := by
  simp only [gluedSubmodule, LinearMap.mem_ker, LinearMap.sub_apply, sub_eq_zero,
    funext_iff, deltaLeft, deltaRight, LinearMap.pi_apply, LinearMap.coe_comp,
    Function.comp_apply, LinearMap.proj_apply, AlgHom.toLinearMap_apply]

/-- The glued colength module, as a type. -/
noncomputable abbrev Glued : Type u := ↥A.gluedSubmodule

/-! ### The certificate -/

/-- **The colength certificate** (worksheet §1.1 (c1)/(c2) in the spec-dd-1 §1c frozen
spelling): chart-local colengths finite projective over `R` (c1); the glued module
finite projective of constant fibre rank `n` — honest finrank at every prime through
`Module.rankAtStalk` (c2); and the two flat-cokernel clauses (c3)/(c4) that make
certificates base-change along ARBITRARY test maps (trivial over a field; transported
by right-exactness; consumed by `FlatCokernel.tensorKer_bijective_of_flat_coker`). -/
structure IsCertified (n : ℕ) : Prop where
  /-- (c1) Each chart-local colength module is a finite `R`-module. -/
  finite_colength : ∀ j, Module.Finite R (A.colength j)
  /-- (c1) Each chart-local colength module is projective over `R`. -/
  projective_colength : ∀ j, Module.Projective R (A.colength j)
  /-- (c2) The glued colength module is a finite `R`-module. -/
  finite_glued : Module.Finite R A.Glued
  /-- (c2) The glued colength module is projective over `R`. -/
  projective_glued : Module.Projective R A.Glued
  /-- (c2) The glued colength module has constant fibre rank `n`. -/
  rankAtStalk_glued : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, Module.rankAtStalk A.Glued p = n
  /-- (c3) The cokernel of `W(d) ↪ Π_j colength j` is flat. -/
  flat_coker_incl : Module.Flat R (A.chartProd ⧸ A.gluedSubmodule)
  /-- (c4) The cokernel of the difference arrow is flat. -/
  flat_coker_diff :
    Module.Flat R (A.ovlProd ⧸ LinearMap.range (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight))

end DivisorAdaptation

/-! ## The certified family and the divisor-functor value -/

variable (n : ℕ)

/-- **A certified divisor family of degree `n` over the test ring `R`** (the worksheet's
(D1) pair `(d, c)`): a local-equation system with a certified finite chart
adaptation. -/
structure CertifiedDivisorFamily [IsAffineHom π] : Type u where
  /-- The local-equation system on the relative curve. -/
  eqns : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations
  /-- The finite chart adaptation refining it. -/
  adaptation : DivisorAdaptation C R π eqns
  /-- The colength certificate of degree `n`. -/
  certified : adaptation.IsCertified n

/-- The divisor-equality setoid on certified families: the underlying local-equation
systems cut the same divisor (`Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq`); the adaptation and
certificate are per-representative data and do not enter the relation. -/
def divFamSetoid [IsAffineHom π] : Setoid (CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n) where
  r F G := Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq F.eqns G.eqns
  iseqv :=
    ⟨fun F => Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_refl F.eqns,
     fun h => h.symm, fun h h' => h.trans h'⟩

/-- **The divisor-functor value on the affine test `R`** (worksheet §1.1): certified
divisor families of degree `n` up to divisor equality. A `Type u` quotient — the
carrier the affine-opens-limit vehicle ranges over. -/
def DivFam [IsAffineHom π] : Type u := Quotient (divFamSetoid C R π n)

namespace DivFam

variable {C R π n} [IsAffineHom π]

/-- The class of a certified family. -/
def mk (F : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n) : DivFam C R π n :=
  Quotient.mk (divFamSetoid C R π n) F

lemma mk_eq_mk_iff {F G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n} :
    mk F = mk G ↔ Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq F.eqns G.eqns :=
  Quotient.eq (r := divFamSetoid C R π n)

/-- **The Picard class of a divisor family** `𝒪(D)`: well defined on the quotient by
the class laws (`picClass_eq_of_divEq`). This is the Abel hook DAT-C consumes. -/
noncomputable def picClass (F : DivFam C R π n) : (relCurve C R).CechPic :=
  Quotient.lift (fun F : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n => F.eqns.picClass)
    (fun _ _ h => Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass_eq_of_divEq h) F

@[simp]
lemma picClass_mk (F : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n) :
    picClass (mk F) = F.eqns.picClass :=
  rfl

end DivFam

end AlgebraicGeometry

## ADDENDUM 2 (2026-07-25, run 0048) — the certificate lane's satisfiability verdict (BINDING)

ADDENDUM 1 restated DDR-9 against `DivFamZar` and asserted, as item 2, that "the universal
family of DDR-3/4 is honestly certified over each `Z(♦)`-chart ring". That assertion has never
been proved, and this addendum records what is now known about it — three theorems, all
kernel-checked warning-free, all in the default build.

### 1. The per-piece clause is a chart statement

`Picard/DivSchemeCertZarChartTrace.lean` (commit `49866bdd1`). A `FinCoverData` carries a
partition of unity on **each** pinned chart, so the chart-`b` pieces cover all of `V_b` and

  `supportLocus ∩ V_b = ⋃_j (supportLocus ∩ pieces_b j)`.

A finite union of closed sets is closed, hence the assembler's `hnoLeak`
(`isCertified_of_noLeak_kernel_spanning`) implies that **both chart traces are closed in the
relative curve** — a statement in which neither the adaptation nor its pieces appear
(`isClosed_supportLocus_inter_chart_of_forall_noLeak`). Contrapositive
`not_forall_noLeak_of_not_isClosed_chart₀`.

Two consequences bind future work. Refining the cover cannot help: the union of the traces is
the fixed set `supportLocus ∩ V_b`, so a finer cover only imposes more closed-trace
constraints on the same union. And shrinking the base does not move the condition; it restates
it over the smaller base.

### 2. The shape that works: swallow or miss

`Picard/DivSchemeCertZarSwallow.lean` (commit `206967379`). If every piece either contains the
whole support or misses it, `hnoLeak` and clause (c1)-finite follow at every piece with no
fibre, no tube and no packet idempotent. A missing piece has a **unit** equation, so its
colength module vanishes and needs no fibrewise regularity input either.

### 3. The verdict

`Picard/DivSchemeCertZarConn.lean` (commit `40f357de8`). Leak-freeness makes a piece trace
closed and the piece is open, so the trace is **clopen in the support**; a preconnected support
therefore forces it to be empty or total. Hence, for a connected divisor, swallow-or-miss is
not an extra hypothesis — it is what leak-freeness already says — and with `relCover_sup`:

> `supportLocus_subset_chart_of_isPreconnected` : a connected divisor whose adaptation is
> leak-free at every piece satisfies `supportLocus ⊆ V₀` **or** `supportLocus ⊆ V₁`.

So `IsCertified`, whose clause (c1) forces leak-freeness, is satisfiable for a connected
divisor **only** if that divisor avoids `π⁻¹(0)` or avoids `π⁻¹(∞)`. Base localization cannot
repair this, because it does not disconnect the divisor: `Spec (R[x]/(x²−t))` over `R = k[t]`
is connected over every basic open of `Spec R`. The I-0209 clopen-packet programme is therefore
available exactly when the divisor is already chart-confined.

### 4. What this obliges the DD-R design to decide

Exactly one question, and it is a design question, not a lemma hunt:

**Does the `Z(♦)` chart confine its divisors to a single pinned chart of `π`?**

* **If yes** — then ADDENDUM 1 item 2 is correct and the remaining certificate work is
  bookkeeping: build the two-piece-per-chart adaptation (a swallowing piece plus its comaximal
  complement, via `DivisorAdaptation.ofAnchors`), and the Čech complex then has at most one
  nontrivial piece per chart, so clauses (c2)/(c3)/(c4) — hence `hinj`, which is *provably*
  clause (c4) — should be free rather than proved. That is roadmap leaf
  `…certificate.cert-collapse`, and it is the single highest-value experiment in the lane: if
  it lands, `away-kerspan` is retired, not solved.
* **If no** — then the atlas must add the avoidance as a carve (it is an open condition, so a
  carve is legitimate), **or** `IsCertified`/`DivFamZar` must be redesigned, because a functor
  that cannot see chart-crossing divisors is not the divisor functor and `divRep` against it
  would represent the wrong thing.

The theta side is the tractable half of the yes-case: `K ⊆ H⁰(Θᵃ)` with `Θ = π⁻¹(∞)`, and a
